chapter: Pedal points, Hampton, Norvo and Debut
title: Lloyd Reese's way of teaching
summary: Reese made them listen to Stravinsky and name the instruments, predicting Mingus would be an arranger.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Learning your horn: teachers, lessons and fees

blocks.x: long. (inaudible.) Yeah, he was, yeah. You also mentioned Lloyd Reese, too, as somebody -- I don't think you really dwelled on it at all.
A teacher Reese can't help but be an influence.
But his way of teaching was so varied. I mean, he made us (inaudible) listen to He made us listen to Stravinsky, in fact. Not By just listening; he said, "Hear the flutes?

Piccolos? What's the clarinet doing there?" I said, "What clarinet, man? Say, "Can't you hear the clarinet players?" I said, "Yeah, I hear them. Play it again, you know?" He said, "Well, what do you think they're doing?" So I'd fool around and try to do it on the piano. And he said, "You're going to be a good arranger someday." "That's what you gotta do; you gotta see what you've been (inaudible) see these guys are doing. They'll be out here a long time with all the credits." He says, "We do those things like that, too."
